issue.title: `ml_get: invalid lnum` when redrawing with visual selection active
issue.body:
### Steps to reproduce

```vim
call setline(1, ['a', 'b'])
new | wincmd p
call feedkeys("G\<C-V>", 'txn')
call win_execute(winnr('#')->win_getid(), 'redraw')
```

When switching to the new buffer which is being viewed by the previous window in this example, the global visual selection state still refers to the selected range in the original buffer, which is out-of-bounds for the new buffer.

While this example uses `win_execute`, maybe this is also possible in places that use `aucmd_prepbuf`, for example? (like with Neovim's `nvim_buf_call`: https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/16937)

### Expected behaviour

No error (visual selection in original buffer should also remain unchanged).

### Version of Vim

8.2.4014

### Environment

OS: Fedora 35
Term: GNOME Terminal 3.42.2
$TERM: `xterm-256color`

### Logs and stack traces

```shell
E315: ml_get: invalid lnum: 2
```

body:
Now fixed in Vim in https://github.com/vim/vim/commit/18f4740f043b353abe47b7a00131317052457686, but given that `nvim_buf_call` uses `aucmd_prepbuf`, it might need an extra change?

Yup:

```vim
call setline(1, ['a', 'b'])
new | wincmd p
call feedkeys("G\<C-V>", 'txn')
autocmd User Explode ++once redraw
doautoall User Explode
```

Also need to make sure this Nvim-specific case works after porting:
```vim
call setline(1, ['a', 'b'])
call feedkeys("G\<C-V>", 'txn')
call win_execute(0, 'call nvim_win_set_buf(0, nvim_create_buf(0, 1)) | redraw')
```

This fix also doesn't handle this case:

```vim
enew | new
call setline(1, ['a', 'b'])
wincmd p
call feedkeys("\<C-V>", 'txn')
call win_execute(winnr('#')->win_getid(), 'call feedkeys("G\<C-V>", ''txn'')')
```

https://github.com/vim/vim/commit/18f4740f043b353abe47b7a00131317052457686
https://github.com/vim/vim/commit/e664a327014f4aa8baf8549a34a4caab2f3116a3
https://github.com/vim/vim/commit/cb1956d6f2aece8ad93e19e5d4c7e0b5e405f056

Let's see if this is enough. :thinking:

issue.body:
### Problem

^ title.

### Steps to reproduce

`nvim --clean -u minimal.lua`

```lua
-- minimal.lua

local selection_anchor = function()
  local _, anchor_row, anchor_col, _ = unpack(vim.fn.getpos("v"))
  return { anchor_row, anchor_col }
end

local feedkeys = function(keys)
  local replaced = vim.api.nvim_replace_termcodes(keys, true, false, true)
  vim.api.nvim_feedkeys(replaced, "x", false)
end

feedkeys("iHello<Esc>bv<Right>")

local anchor = selection_anchor()
local anchor_in_buf = vim.api.nvim_buf_call(0, selection_anchor)

assert(vim.deep_equal(anchor, { 1, 1 }))
-- 💥 is actually { 1, 2 }.
assert(vim.deep_equal(anchor_in_buf, { 1, 1 }))
```

### Expected behavior

`getpos("v")` returns the same value even if wrapped in `nvim_buf_call`.

### Nvim version (nvim -v)

NVIM v0.12.0-nightly+8e8f452

### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same?

N/A

### Operating system/version

macOS 15.0

### Terminal name/version

alacritty 

### $TERM environment variable

alacritty

### Installation

nixpkgs
